definition: A proposition P : Prop holds when a proof term inhabits P in the encoded logic. ∃ P : Prop, P asks for a proposition together with a proof; ¬∀ P : Prop, ¬P denies universal failure. Neither formula introduces an external truth predicate or says truth is independent of endorsement.
note: This is the pilot’s explicit logical reading, using Lean’s propositions-as-types convention. It is not identified with ontological, robust, minimal, or attitude-independent truth; those transitions need separate interpretation bridges.
